## v3 — 2026-06-11 · live
framing: two-track AI story is the spine — pull the Engage/Execute/Extend structure
sources:
  - janet-5-27-transcript
  - carol-deck#p12-18

The point-of-view report reframes Infoblox's AI position as a two-track story.
Track one is the IQ layer — the protective intelligence already embedded in the
product. Track two is the MCP/API layer that lets agents act on that intelligence.
Together they answer "why Infoblox, why now" without leaning on a single feature.

The narrative backbone is Engage / Execute / Extend. Engage frames the threat and
the buyer's stake; Execute shows the product doing the work today; Extend points at
the agentic future the APIs unlock. Carol's deck (p12–18) supplies the proof points
that hang under each verb, and Janet's 5/27 framing locks the leadership voice.

The deliverable is a 14–18 slide report the field can carry into Engage/Execute/Extend
conversations without re-deriving the story each time. It is the keystone artifact the
6/11 workshop builds on.

## v2 — 2026-04-23 · superseded
framing: core-team synthesis pass
sources:
  - kickoff-transcript

The first synthesis pass treated the report as a product overview: a feature tour
with a security framing bolted on top. It catalogued capabilities but never resolved
them into a single buyer-facing argument, so every slide competed for the same attention.

This version served its purpose as a forcing function — it surfaced that we were missing
a spine — but it was superseded once the two-track thesis emerged from the 5/27 session.
